claims.text: High-temperature structural and chemical stability of high-entropy nanoalloys is governed by formation of a stable, coherent interface between constituent elements.
A coherent interface suppresses atomic diffusion in high-entropy nanoalloys.
A coherent interface suppresses elemental segregation in high-entropy nanoalloys.
The initial high-entropy nanoalloy has a uniform distribution of constituent elements.
High-temperature annealing is expected to yield or preserve a coherent interface between the alloy elements.
Annealed high-entropy nanoalloys will exhibit improved structural stability relative to unannealed high-entropy nanoalloys.
Annealed high-entropy nanoalloys will exhibit improved chemical stability relative to unannealed high-entropy nanoalloys.
Annealed high-entropy nanoalloys will show reduced atomic diffusion relative to the unannealed baseline.
Annealed high-entropy nanoalloys will show reduced elemental segregation relative to the unannealed baseline.
The prediction applies in an inert atmosphere from 500 to 1000 °C for annealing times up to 100 hours.
